note: Adapted from the original English description of Snyder 1924 (new species, Leucotermes convexinotatus Snyder, type locality Colón, Panama; later placed in Heterotermes). The original also describes the soldier and the worker; the passages available here cover the alate. Note 12 of the original states that the characters separating this species from L. crinitus Emerson MS. are taken from Emerson's manuscript.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: New species (originally Leucotermes convexinotatus, later placed in Heterotermes). Type locality Colón, Panama. The alate is paler than L. tenuis; the head nearly oval, widest at the compound eyes and narrower than in tenuis; the fontanelle smaller than in tenuis, a pale, slightly raised round spot on the line behind the compound eyes; antennae 17-segmented; postclypeus distinctly convex, more than 3 times as wide as long, the posterior margin distinctly convex, with a deeper concavity between it and the margin of the head than in tenuis; pronotum nearly heart-shaped, the middle of the anterior margin concave, the posterior margin not concave.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head yellowish brown, darker between the compound eyes, paler posteriorly and less dark than in L. tenuis Hagen; nearly oval, widest at the compound eyes and narrower than in tenuis, rounded posteriorly; covered with rather dense long pale yellow setae and short hairs. Fontanelle smaller than in tenuis, a pale, slightly raised round spot on the line behind the compound eyes. Antennae pale yellowish brown, 17-segmented, with short hairs, the segments varying in size and shape; first segment long, cylindrical; second shorter and not wide; third ring-like, about half the length of the second; fourth longer than the third; the following segments gradually wider and more wedge-shaped towards the tip; last segment long, slender, elliptical. Compound eyes black, not round, not very protruding; their distance from the lateral margin of the head less than their long diameter. Ocelli present or absent; when present, elongated, their distance from the compound eyes about equal to their short diameter. Labrum pale yellow, longer than wide, widest near the middle, slightly linguiform, broadly rounded in front, with long hairs at the tip. Postclypeus pale yellow, bulging convexly as in tenuis, more than 3 times as wide as long; the posterior margin distinctly convex, the concavity of the margin of the head deeper than in tenuis; the postclypeus longer than in tenuis but not so wide; not so distinctly bilobed as in tenuis. Pronotum concolorous with the head, nearly heart-shaped, wider than long but not so wide as the head, the posterior margin not concave, the middle of the anterior margin concave; surface and margins with long setae and short hairs.
